page.layout: One printed page. One main text column on the left, with a black-letter marginal note block on the right beside the first lines. Running head top left, page number top right. Signature "E 2" and catchword "nugere," at the foot.

main_text.p: tinuaret, quando, quoties, quandiu placeret: editus verò, successorvé datus apud præfe-ctum subvrbanum Episcopi ministrum jura-ret: juramenti summa hæc esset, JUS ET JUSTITIAM SE ADMINISTRA-TURUM OMNIBUS INTEGRE ATQUE INCORRUPTE, SECUN-DUM MOREM FORI ISTIUS: præfectofubvrbano ultra triduum tergiver-sante, consuli potestas esset hoc juramentum ab eo recipere eâdem verborum formâ. Pro hoc jure civitas quotannis aureos scutatos Francicos XXVIII penderet Episcopo ipsi Vltrajecti, & vigesimo quoquo anno marcas duas argenti puri cum marcâ triente præfecto Coverdio Coverdia: utrumque ante exitum Octobris: Et hæc pactio vim haberet in annos C. quibus finitis, si civitas ante exitum ejusdem Octobris offerret Episcopo marcas argenti similis XVI, & trientem marcarum duarum, peteretq; ejusdem juris & pacti continuationem, eadem omnia valerent in annos totidem: & ab eorum sine rursum repetitis ijsdem, & pactis purè servatis in annos totidem alios atque alios: idq; extenderetur in perpetuum, nec liceret episcopis ab-Dat he mallick oꝛdel vñ recht doe vnde weder-baren laten sal na olden heyrka-men des gerichtes in Groningen.

page.notes: The first line of the text begins mid-word ("tinuaret") and is a fragment from the previous page. Italic and roman type were judged from the scan and may be imperfect. Small capitals (JUS ET JUSTITIAM, XXVIII, XVI) are given in capitals. The black-letter note on the right is partly illegible at its edges and some words are uncertain, so it is not checked letter by letter; the reading "heyrka-men" and "laten" are doubtful. The catchword "nugere," stands at the right below the last line, and "ab-" is the printed half word at the line end. "Coverdio Coverdia" may be a printed catchword or name repetition. "paẽti" in the line "pacti" is uncertain and may be a ligature or abbreviation.
